opportunities.title: Publish an llms.txt, given the platform's underlying markup investment is already thorough
opportunities.rationale: No llms.txt exists (a genuine 404). Every sampled article carried a complete SocialMediaPosting JSON-LD node (headline, dates, full author and publisher graphs), so the underlying capability to describe content in machine-readable terms is clearly already built -- an llms.txt pointing agents at sitemap structure or licensing terms (already declared separately at /license.xml) would be a small, low-cost extension of work already done.
opportunities.mechanism: A short llms.txt naming the platform's own sitemap index and license terms gives a well-behaved agent a documented entry point beyond relying on sitemap discovery alone.
steps: Add a minimal llms.txt referencing the existing sitemap index and license.xml.

not_assessed.check: Answerability, freshness/corroboration, and engagement across a broader sample; structured-data consistency across Medium's other content surfaces (publications, tag pages, member-only/paywalled articles)
not_assessed.reason: This run hand-verified robots.txt policy and structured-data completeness on five sampled articles rather than running the full sampled-page probe. Content quality on a user-generated platform is inherently variable per-author; the five samples checked all happened to carry complete markup, which is a real, verified result for those samples but not a claim about the platform's full content diversity.
not_assessed.impact: Cannot state a general answerability coverage figure or confirm markup completeness holds for paywalled ('member-only') stories specifically, which this run did not target.
